claims.summary: Over a field k, let X_t be a finitely generated FI-set of variables (every variable in the image of X_s for s<=r) and Gamma_t polynomial systems on X_t such that every injection carries the axioms of degree <=D of Gamma_t into the degree-D closure of Gamma_t'. Then the induced substitutions carry closures into closures; the windows Q_t = V_K/(C_D cap V_K) form an FI-module generated in degree <=rK; for fixed polynomials F on a fixed index set with deg w + K <= D the common kernels form a sub-FI-module under injections fixing it; by Church-Ellenberg-Farb-Nagpal (arXiv 1210.1854, its Noetherian property and polynomial-dimension theorems) both dimensions are eventually polynomial over any field. The product and functional pigeonhole systems at fixed holes are such families in the pigeons; holes are functorial contravariantly by setting new variables to 0. For the product pigeonhole systems with K<D<=n the windows have the basis of distinct-hole monomials, dim Q_m = sum_{s<=min(K,n)} binom(n,s) m^s for every m, and along the diagonal m=t+1, n=t the hole-axiom windows form an FI-module agreeing with Q for t>=D, of dimension sum_{s<=K} binom(t,s)(t+1)^s there.
claims.assessment: Working proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer; the restricted hypothesis, the corrected hole direction and the exact inert-regime count are its corrections.
claims.rationale: Turns finite checks at a fixed number of holes into eventually polynomial families of window and kernel dimensions; no explicit range is given.
